item.title: Monkey Dies At Oregon Experimentation Facility Following Medication Failure
item.description: Portland, OR — The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has cited Oregon Health & Science University’s (OHSU) Oregon National Primate Research Center (ONPRC) for violating the Animal Welfare Act after a rhesus macaque died following the abrupt discontinuation of long-term steroid treatment.

item.title: New Poll: Almost Half of US Adults Unaware of Connection Between Processed Meat Consumption and Colorectal Cancer
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Just before National Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month begins in March, a new Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine/Morning Consult poll found that nearly half of Americans aren’t aware that eating processed meat increases the risk of developing colorectal cancer.

item.title: Ozempic Aftermath: Why Most People Regain Weight (And How to Prevent It)
item.description: Millions of Americans are turning to GLP-1 weight loss medications like Ozempic and Wegovy. But here’s the question few are asking: What happens when you stop?

item.title: The Physicians Committee Applauds NIH-Wide Efforts to Support Human-Based Research Coordination and Infrastructure
item.description: In a public comment to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Physicians Committee experts expressed support for two recent actions the agency has taken toward implementing the human-based initiative launched in 2025 and made recommendations for building on this exciting progress.

item.title: After Years of Pressure from Legislators and Physicians, Brown University Replaces Animals in Deadly Training Exercises
item.description: PROVIDENCE, R.I.—After years of demands from Rhode Island state legislators and physicians, Brown University ended its deadly use of animals for training emergency medicine physicians.

item.title: The Physicians Committee Engages With NIH Center on Strategies to Promote Human-Based Translational Research
item.description: The Physicians Committee recently made recommendations to the National Center for Advancing Translational Science (NCATS) at the National Institutes of Health to prioritize human-based research and reduce animal experimentation as a part of a broader agency-wide initiative.

item.title: Physicians Committee Advocates for Human-Based Neurology Research
item.description: Studying the human brain is an extraordinary frontier, but unlocking its secrets requires the right tools. This Brain Awareness Week (March 16-22, 2026), the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine is championing a shift to human-based brain research. By using human cells and patient data over animals, we can accelerate new treatments through more accurate modelling—and spare animal lives.
